The 4% Rule Explained: Safe Retirement Withdrawals & Capital Longevity

📅 Updated September 2026 ⏱ 7 Min Read ✍️ Finmatrix Financial Engineering Research Desk

Trinity Study Safe Withdrawal Rates & Sequence of Returns Risk

The Safe Withdrawal Rate (SWR) Model: In 1994, financial planner William Bengen published landmark research analyzing historical 30-year rolling market cycles back to 1926. He demonstrated that an initial 4.0% withdrawal adjusted annually for CPI inflation never depleted a balanced equity/bond portfolio.

30-Year Success Rate: 95% to 98% portfolio survival across all historical 30-year sequences, including the Great Depression and 1970s stagflation.
Extended Horizons (40–50 Years): For FIRE early retirees, adjusting the SWR to 3.25%–3.50% (28.5x–30.8x expenses) shields against early-decade market drawdowns.

"The single greatest threat to a retirement portfolio is not long-term inflation, but severe market declines during the first five years of withdrawals (Sequence of Returns Risk)." — William Bengen, CFP®.

Authoritative Citations: Trinity University Retirement Study (Cooley, Hubbard, Walz); Journal of Financial Planning (Vol. 7, No. 4).

"A 4% initial withdrawal rate from a portfolio containing 50% to 75% large-cap US equities and 25% to 50% intermediate corporate bonds has historically provided a 98% success rate over a 30-year retirement horizon."
— The Trinity Study (Cooley, Hubbard, and Walz, Trinity University)

How Much Can You Safely Withdraw in Retirement?

Based on the landmark 1998 Trinity Study, the 4% rule states that a retiree with a diversified portfolio of 50% to 75% stocks and high-grade bonds can withdraw 4.00% of their initial portfolio balance in Year 1. In subsequent years, that initial dollar amount is adjusted upward by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) annual inflation rate.

How to Calculate Your Target Retirement Goal (25x Rule)

To determine the exact capital required to retire under the 4% rule, divide your annual spending by 0.04 (or multiply annual expenses by 25).

Target Nest Egg = Annual Living Expenses × 25

Worked Example: If your household requires $60,000 per year in living expenses:

  • Initial Target Portfolio: $60,000 × 25 = $1,500,000
  • Year 1 Withdrawal: $1,500,000 × 4% = $60,000 ($5,000/month)
  • Year 2 Withdrawal (assuming 3% CPI inflation): $60,000 × 1.03 = $61,800

Historical Success Rates: 30 vs 40-Year Time Horizons

Portfolio Asset Allocation 4% Rate (30 Years) 4% Rate (40 Years) 3.5% Rate (40 Years / FIRE)
100% Equities (S&P 500) 95% Success 88% Success 97% Success
75% Equities / 25% Bonds 98% Success 91% Success 99% Success
50% Equities / 50% Bonds 96% Success 84% Success 98% Success

Adjusting for Early Retirement (FIRE)

If you plan to achieve Financial Independence and Retire Early (FIRE) in your 30s or 40s (requiring a 40 to 55-year capital drawdown horizon), modern financial research recommends adjusting to a 3.25% to 3.50% safe withdrawal rate (a 28.5x to 30x expense multiplier) to eliminate Sequence of Returns Risk.
